visualReview.executedBy: Codex; every listed screenshot displayed with view_image and inspected
findings: All three actual desktop reference cards at 1440×1000 and all three native mobile landscape fullscreen reference pages at 844×390 retain the complete original source titles, quoted sentences and source locators. Both rows fit, and native controls do not cover source text.

All three 390px article screenshots show readable original titles/excerpts/locators and wrapping source links without horizontal overflow. Cache-consistency article now retains the exact raw-English locators in references.json; its h3 R1/R2 headings are valid citation identities.

All three videos actually played at 1x from 0.2 seconds before the new appendix through ended, beyond their original AAC endpoints. Each reference page was observed during playback. Only these three changed videos were fetched; earlier completed batches were not repeated.

All 24 painted seek checks (exact first frame, first+0.1ms, middle and last frame for each page in both viewports) were paused with no active native caption. Original body SHA, full decoded-frame/audio preservation receipts, published storyboard, chapter identities/starts and first-publication dates passed the local checks.
No browser console/page/media errors or horizontal page overflow were observed.
limitations: Chromium viewport emulation, not physical mobile/iOS Safari.
Only the three changed appendices play at 1x on desktop; no duplicate mobile plays or prior-batch media GETs.
Playback is muted; no human audio/ASR claim. Complete body preservation uses the baseline-SHA-bound full media receipts.
390px embedded video remains small; full reading is inspected in actual native fullscreen at 844×390 and article text.
Citation clicks prevent navigation; source verification is a separate record.
visualReview.scope: UI/paused-card/appendix playback review only. Source GETs and source authenticity are recorded in the independent source audits; no repeated source GET or speech-listening claim.
